correctness.rationale: For n>=3, grounded principal Laplacian L_FF of K_{n,n} minus link (a,b) is SPD. Decomposition into degree-eigenvalue within-group contrasts and a <=4-dimensional equitable quotient H gives J(S)=sum_g (r_g-1)/d_g +tr H^{-1}. Every unordered two-leader set belongs to one of five objective classes, whose rational formulas are in the actual RESULT.md. Subtractions J1,J2,J3>J0 have positive polynomials for n>=3. Remaining J0−J4=(n³−6n²+5n−1)/(n(n−1)²(2n−1)), with f(3)=f(4)=−13, f(5)=−1, f(6)=29 and f(n+1)−f(n)=3n(n−3)>0 for n>=4, so only missing-link endpoints win n=3..5, while exactly (n−1)(n−2) ordinary same-side pairs win all n>=6. Independently constructed exact rational grounded Laplacians and checked all two-leader pairs for n=3..10 (708 pairs), including n=3 empty-group boundary. This finite check is not an infinite proof; exact quotient and sign identities are.
residual_risks: Unit edge conductance, exactly two pinned noise-free leaders and balanced bipartitions; other disturbances/multiple missing links are outside claim.

value.rationale: A single-link fault switches the best two pinned leaders between two qualitatively different symmetry types exactly at n=6, unlike intact complete bipartite graphs. The exact all-n optimum and multiplicity give a natural fault-sensitivity benchmark for graph-constrained noisy consensus; the near-tie 1/720 at n=5 makes exact sign analysis useful, not an arbitrary tiny improvement.
residual_risks: The model is homogeneous and uses precisely two noise-free leaders; no robustness to arbitrary multiple edge failures.
